sentences.text: For binary-additive F_8 codes with 256 messages, C-15 deduces n_2(8,3;11) ≤ 88 and n_2(8,3;15) ≤ 120 from published divisible-code classifications, refining the endpoints 89 and 121 of Kurz, arXiv:2412.14615v3, Theorem 17.
Together with constructions already known when C-15 was written, those upper bounds leave only the intervals 87–88 and 119–120.

C-33 replaces the length-46 and length-74 classification inputs of that deduction by a dimension-free argument: every binary 16-divisible code of either length has even column multiplicities and maximum multiplicity at least 16, so Gamma_2(16,46)=Gamma_2(16,74)=16.
The divisible-code length criteria and classification tables used for these upper bounds are those identified in C-20.
C-30 then excludes a code of length 88, size 256 and minimum distance at least 77, and with the lower end of C-15 concludes n_2(8,3;11)=87.
Existence of a binary-additive F_8 code of length 120, size 256 and minimum distance 105 is not settled by the verified claims.

C-28 proves only necessary conditions: any such code has a realization by 120 three-dimensional coordinate subspaces whose defect multiset is 16-divisible of length 105, has maximum multiplicity at most 15 and span dimension 7 or 8, meets every point in at most four subspaces, and has an 8-divisible hyperplane section of length 41.
C-33's multiplicity theorem concerns effective lengths 46 and 74, not the length-105 defect arising in that necessary-condition reduction.

sections.heading: Published separations and what remains open

sentences.text: C-19 records published additive quaternary codes with parameters [33,4,24], [36,4,26] and [40,4,29], each with 4^4 codewords, whose distances exceed the best F_4-linear codes of the same length and dimension 4, which have distances 23, 25 and 28.
None of the verified claims constructs a new additive code, and none solves the full problem of beating linear codes at small distance or of extending Griesmer-type bounds to other metrics.
There is a (41,12,5) covering with 2046 blocks, so C(41,12,5) ≤ 2046, improving the earlier verified bound of 2207.
There is a (70,25,3) covering with 37 blocks, so C(70,25,3) ≤ 37.
There is a (85,24,3) covering with 76 blocks, so C(85,24,3) ≤ 76.
There is a (53,20,3) covering with 34 blocks, so C(53,20,3) ≤ 34.
There is a (61,25,3) covering with 27 blocks, so C(61,25,3) ≤ 27.
There is a (16,8,5) covering with 114 blocks, so C(16,8,5) ≤ 114.
No verified claim produces a (16,8,5) covering with 113 or fewer blocks; the best verified upper bound remains 114.

For G=F_2^4 and H={0,...,7}, any H-invariant family that splits a full G-orbit has translation stabilizer exactly H, and otherwise the stabilizer is G; every odd-sized H-invariant family, and hence any H-invariant 113-block covering, must split the orbit {H, H xor 8}.
If such a 113-block covering is also irredundant, it must split at least one further full G-orbit of size 8 or 16.
These symmetry statements are conditional and do not decide whether C(16,8,5) is 114 or smaller.
